closed.note: Recorded retroactively when the sticky ledger shipped. The FAIL itself has been open since the 2026-08-08 daily run — the baseline has been pinned at 2026-08-07T18:23:51Z ever since, which is what record_baseline refusing to advance a failing slice looks like. Left to the previous code this incident would have been adopted as the new normal by the 2026-08-22 run, when the pinned baseline passed MAX_BASELINE_AGE_DAYS. `detail` and `observed_at_open` are the reading from ops_status.py [3] on 2026-08-10; `entries` there is the baseline's 43,341 plus the +18 the check reported, not a separately fetched figure. docs/HANDOFF.md #29 item 1 has the full account.
closed.reason: Traced to daily_classification_spotcheck.py, which sampled the 15 largest rows by job_count and auto-applied model-confirmed country relabels with no magnitude bound, no cap and no human. On 2026-08-08 it moved three ERM rows off 'Multiple countries' to 'United States'. Reverted 2026-08-12T01:51Z; the public corrections log records 'ERM country reverted to the value Eurofound records', 144,000 jobs across 3 rows, all three factsheets stating Country = World. Only 92,000 of that 144,000 could ever move THIS headline: Citigroup 52,000 already sat inside the country_basis=any slice through its employer_country=United States HQ stamp, so relabelling its job-location country added nothing here. General Motors 47,000 + Cinemaworld 45,000 = 92,000 moved, plus 1,210 of legitimate arrivals on +18 entries, which is the +93,210 this incident recorded. Mechanism bounded in 68bd698: AUTO_APPLY_MAX_JOBS=5000, any country relabel off a worldwide label refused at any size, enforced in the function that POSTs. Replacement baseline measured live 2026-08-12: +9,433 jobs over 4.4d against a floor of 88,019.

note: Open headline incidents, read by data_integrity.MovementInvariant. A slice listed under `open` reports FAIL regardless of what today's numbers say — that is the point: the movement formula's own inputs (elapsed span, arriving rows, baseline age) all widen over time, so an incident left to the calendar closes itself. Do not hand-edit this file. Close an incident with `python3 data_integrity.py --close-incident <slice> --reviewed-by ... --reason ... --rows ... --replacement-jobs ... --replacement-entries ...`, which is the only path that also writes the replacement baseline.

This is true however many entries arrived, which is why the movement guard's allowance cannot see it. Check the last reconcile-supersets run, any country/AI relabel job, and the corrections log
